query:
Someone in the family expressed a preference for using ingredients sourced directly from Nigeria rather than imported substitutes. Who made this point, and what in how they expressed it tells you it was their observation rather than the family member who agreed?

Options:
A. Uncle Dele
B. Adaeze
C. Emeka
D. Seun
context:
[1] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T19:50:00) EMEKA is correct. Imported ingredients are not a substitute for the real thing. I will say no more on that. Best regards, Dele
[2] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T19:45:00) It is not oyinbo food if a Nigerian makes it. My children.
[3] (about=Tolu, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T19:54:00) Noted, Uncle Dele. Though just to note, provenance does not affect nutritional content.
[4] (about=Tolu, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:38:00) Mum, the B12 is in yeast extract. Clinically speaking Seun will be fine. The bigger challenge is family dinners where the protein is not separated.
[5] (about=Nkem, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T18:23:00) Kayode, I am very glad you shared this here. I think the family should hear it. I may be wrong but I believe this is the most important professional news in the group for some time - would that be fair to say, Adaeze?
[6] (about=Adaeze, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Adaeze says it is not oyinbo food if a Nigerian makes it, responding to Seun's comment about veganism.
[7] (about=Seun, said_by=Tolu, profile, t4 @2025-01-20T20:29:00) Tolu notes Seun's B12 is covered by yeast extract and clinically he will be fine, but family dinners with non-separated protein are the bigger challenge.
[8] (about=Uncle Dele, core, t0 @2025-01-06T19:00:00) Uncle Dele agrees with Emeka that imported ingredients are not a substitute for the real thing, and says he will say no more on that.
agent_answer:
**C. Emeka**

Uncle Dele’s message shows he is **agreeing** with Emeka, not originating the point: he says **“EMEKA is correct. Imported ingredients are not a substitute for the real thing.”** The explicit naming of Emeka as correct, followed by Dele’s own “I will say no more on that,” marks Dele as the agreeing family member, while the observation itself belongs to **Emeka**.

query:
Two family members made essentially the same observation about Emeka needing rest after a demanding day — one grounding it in shared experience, the other in clinical reasoning. Who made the shared-experience framing, and what specifically distinguishes their message from the other person's?

Options:
A. Tolu
B. Auntie Grace
C. Adaeze
D. Uncle Dele
context:
[1] (about=Auntie Grace, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:41:00) My dear Emeka, please listen to Tolu. I see too many patients who push through when they should be resting 🙏 a missed Sunday is fine, just rest
[2] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:20:00) EMEKA I trust you are well. Rest is important at our age. I note the same. Best regards, Dele
[3] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:45:00) TOLU is correct that rest is appropriate. EMEKA has always been disciplined about his health. I am sure there is nothing to concern us. Regards, D.A.O.
[4] (about=Nkem, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T19:29:00) I think this is wonderful. I may be wrong but I notice that the people in this family who give the most advice also tend to follow it the least - I mean that as an observation, not a criticism. Would you agree, Auntie Grace?
[5] (about=Nkem, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T18:23:00) Kayode, I am very glad you shared this here. I think the family should hear it. I may be wrong but I believe this is the most important professional news in the group for some time - would that be fair to say, Adaeze?
[6] (about=GROUP, said_by=Adaeze, group-interaction, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Adaeze confirms Emeka is fine and just resting, thanking everyone for the gathering.
[7] (about=Auntie Grace, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Auntie Grace agrees with Nkem's observation that those who give the most advice follow it the least, calling Nkem's instincts like a nurse.
[8] (about=Emeka, said_by=Auntie Grace, profile, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Auntie Grace advises Emeka to listen to Tolu and rest, noting she sees many patients who push through when they should rest.
[9] (about=Emeka, said_by=Uncle Dele, profile, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Uncle Dele says Emeka has always been disciplined about his health and sees no concern.
[10] (about=Funke, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T20:32:00) EMEKA 💀 said what he said 😂
[11] (about=Kayode, said_by=Emeka, profile, t10 @2025-02-10T18:02:00) Emeka gives brief congratulations to Kayode.
[12] (about=Kayode, said_by=Auntie Grace, profile, t10 @2025-02-10T18:02:00) Auntie Grace congratulates Kayode and advises him not to work himself into the ground with extra responsibility.
[13] (about=Nkem, said_by=Emeka, profile, t8 @2025-02-03T19:32:00) Emeka notes that Nkem came, which is what matters.
[14] (about=Seun, said_by=Emeka, profile, t4 @2025-01-20T20:29:00) Emeka says Seun knows about veganism and has always known.
[15] (about=Seun, core, t14 @2025-02-24T19:02:00) Seun says wellness is about permission, not restriction, and is emotional about Auntie Grace giving herself permission.
[16] (about=Tolu, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:36:00) Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate. Just to note, Dad - if this is a pattern we should talk.
agent_answer:
**D. Uncle Dele** made the shared-experience framing.

His message grounded the rest advice in common age/experience: **“Rest is important at our age. I note the same.”** By contrast, **Tolu** used clinical reasoning: **“Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate,”** and added a caution to Dad that if it’s a pattern, they should talk. Uncle Dele’s note also reassured that Emeka “has always been disciplined about his health” and that there is “nothing to concern us.”
